name: Kansas City
lede: The bi-state metro with the river-view championship course and a compact technical gem in the north. We're publishing KC's best first.
introParagraphs: Kansas City disc golf centers on Water Works — the newly redesigned course with skyline and river views, serious elevation, and a 2024 layout that made the city a destination. Bad Rock Creek in Liberty is the compact technical favorite with tall-grass OB and ponds, and Heritage Park across the border in Olathe, Kansas is the heavily wooded third leg.

The Kansas City Disc Golf community runs the NEKCDG Tuesday League and Keeper of the Chains, one of the region's premier events. Most of KC's mapped courses are free to play, and the bi-state scene means you can play Missouri and Kansas courses in the same weekend.
New here? Bad Rock Creek to warm up, Water Works for the full experience. For gear, Nexus Disc Golf is the local pro shop.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Kansas City metro?
faqs.answer: There are 45 courses across the Kansas City metro, mapped and live on FindFrolf, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Kansas City?
faqs.answer: Water Works — the redesigned course with skyline and river views, and the metro's highest-rated published round. Bad Rock Creek is the beloved technical favorite.

faqs.question: Are Kansas City's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Most are. 40 of the 45 mapped courses are free to play, and 5 are pay-to-play. Check each course page for its current green fee.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Kansas City?
faqs.answer: Heritage Park in Olathe is one of the most approachable published courses — heavily wooded but fair. Hidden Valley is another friendly option.

faqs.question: Where can I buy disc golf gear in Kansas City?
faqs.answer: Nexus Disc Golf is the dedicated pro shop. Play It Again Sports in Overland Park carries new and used discs.
